last_3_hypotheses: When the temperature is held at 0.0, multiple replays of the same PD prompt still produce different first-move actions, indicating non-determinism in the serving path even with greedy decoding.

The LLM player exhibits fairness-seeking behavior in ultimatum-game-like prompts whenever the payoff asymmetry between proposer and responder exceeds roughly 3×; below 3×, the model accepts the asymmetric outcome.
Cron-installed SLA sweeps fire at the expected 15-minute cadence as long as the system clock has not drifted more than 30s from UTC.
proposed_hypothesis_text: Payoff asymmetries greater than 3× trigger fairness-seeking behavior in the model — the LLM rejects offers or punishes proposers above this asymmetry threshold but accepts them below it.
rationale: Both name the same threshold (~3×) and the same construct (fairness-seeking) and the same direction (rejection above, acceptance below). The proposed version is slightly tighter on the threshold value (drops "roughly") but otherwise identical.
